name: Hashub
title: Levite Who Renewed the Covenant
summary: Hashub was a Levite who lived in the period after the exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the Levites who took part in the great prayer and covenant renewal when the people returned to Jerusalem. He helped seal the covenant with God on behalf of the people.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Great Prayer
keyEvents.description: Hashub was among the Levites who cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God during the great act of repentance and prayer in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Teaching in the Law
keyEvents.description: Hashub was among the Levites who helped the people understand the Law when Ezra read it aloud to the assembly.

keyEvents.title: The Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Hashub was one of the Levites who placed his seal on the written covenant agreement to follow God's Law.

keyEvents.title: Overseeing the External Work at the Temple
keyEvents.description: Hashub is mentioned in connection with the Levites' service and responsibility for various tasks related to God's house.

keyEvents.title: The People's Renewed Commitment
keyEvents.description: As part of the group of Levites, Hashub helped ensure that the people committed themselves to keeping the Sabbath, paying the temple tax, and following God's commands after returning from exile.
